title: I don't know
summary: Say what you don't know, don't understand or don't speak, with لَا before a verb, and ask for help in class.
intro: To make a present-tense verb negative, put لَا in front of it: أَعْرِفُ (I know) → لَا أَعْرِفُ (I don't know). Nothing else changes. Three phrases will help you every day in class: لَا أَفْهَمُ (I don't understand), مَا مَعْنَى …؟ (what does … mean?) and مَرَّة أُخْرَى، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ (once more, please).
objectives: Say 'I don't know' and 'I don't understand'
Make any present-tense verb negative with لَا
Ask what a word means with مَا مَعْنَى …؟
Say which languages you speak, and which you don't

realLife.title: A hard question
realLife.story: In class Mr Karim asks Daniel what a word means, and Daniel has no idea. Instead of staying silent, he learns to say so in Arabic, to ask what a word means and to ask the teacher to say it again.

dialogue.title: Once more, please!
dialogue.culture: Saying لَا أَعْرِفُ (I don't know) or لَا أَفْهَمُ (I don't understand) is perfectly polite in an Arabic class. Teachers are treated with respect, and students often start a question with يَا أُسْتَاذ (sir) or يَا أُسْتَاذَة (miss).

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، سُؤَال لَكَ: مَا مَعْنَى كَلِمَةِ «مَطَار»؟
lines.en: Daniel, a question for you: what does the word maṭār mean?

lines.ar: مَطَار؟ آسِف يَا أُسْتَاذ، لَا أَعْرِفُ هٰذِهِ الْكَلِمَة.
lines.en: Maṭār? I'm sorry, sir, I don't know this word.

lines.ar: لَا مُشْكِلَة. يَا لَيْلَى، هَلْ تَعْرِفِينَ مَعْنَى «مَطَار»؟
lines.en: No problem. Layla, do you know what maṭār means?

lines.ar: نَعَم! الْمَطَار مَكَان لِلطَّائِرَات، مِثْلُ مَطَارِ الْقَاهِرَة.
lines.en: Yes! An airport is a place for planes, like Cairo Airport.

lines.ar: آهْ! الْآن أَفْهَمُ. شُكْرًا يَا لَيْلَى!
lines.en: Ah! Now I understand. Thank you, Layla!

lines.ar: جَيِّد. يَا طُلَّاب، عِنْدَمَا لَا تَفْهَمُونَ، قُولُوا: لَا أَفْهَمُ!
lines.en: Good. Students, when you don't understand something, say: I don't understand!

lines.ar: يَا أُسْتَاذ، أَنْتَ تَتَكَلَّمُ بِسُرْعَة أَحْيَانًا، وَلَا نَفْهَمُ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَات.
lines.en: Sir, sometimes you speak fast, and we don't understand all the words.

lines.ar: صَحِيح؟ إِذَنْ قُولُوا: «مَرَّة أُخْرَى، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ» أَوْ «بِبُطْء، مِنْ فَضْلِكَ».
lines.en: Really? Then say 'once more, please' or 'slowly, please'.

lines.ar: يَا أُسْتَاذ، عِنْدِي سُؤَال: هَلْ تَتَكَلَّمُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة؟
lines.en: Sir, I have a question: do you speak English?

lines.ar: نَعَم، أَتَكَلَّمُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة وَالْفَرَنْسِيَّة، لٰكِنْ فِي الصَّفّ نَتَكَلَّمُ الْعَرَبِيَّة فَقَطْ!
lines.en: Yes, I speak English and French, but in class we speak only Arabic!

lines.ar: وَأَنَا لَا أَتَكَلَّمُ الْفَرَنْسِيَّة. هَلْ هِيَ صَعْبَة يَا أُسْتَاذ؟
lines.en: And I don't speak French. Is it difficult, sir?

lines.ar: كُلُّ لُغَة صَعْبَة فِي الْبِدَايَة، ثُمَّ سَهْلَة مَعَ الْوَقْت.
lines.en: Every language is hard at the beginning, and then it gets easy with time.

lines.ar: وَالْعَرَبِيَّة؟ مَتَى هِيَ سَهْلَة؟ أَنَا لَا أَعْرِفُ!
lines.en: And Arabic? When does it get easy? I really don't know!

lines.ar: يَا دَانْيَال، أَنْتَ تَدْرُسُ كُلَّ يَوْم، وَتَفْهَمُ أَكْثَرَ كُلَّ أُسْبُوع.
lines.en: Daniel, you study every day, and you understand more every week.

lines.ar: صَحِيح يَا لَيْلَى. وَالْآن، الْوَاجِب لِلْغَد: عَشْر كَلِمَات جَدِيدَة.
lines.en: That's right, Layla. And now, the homework for tomorrow: ten new words.

reading.title: Daniel's languages
reading.ar: أَنَا أَتَكَلَّمُ الْإِنْجِلِيزِيَّة، وَأَتَكَلَّمُ الْعَرَبِيَّة قَلِيلًا. لَا أَتَكَلَّمُ الْفَرَنْسِيَّة. أَفْهَمُ الْأُسْتَاذ كَرِيم، لٰكِنْ لَا أَفْهَمُ كُلَّ الْكَلِمَات. الْعَرَبِيَّة صَعْبَة، لٰكِنَّهَا جَمِيلَة!
reading.en: I speak English, and I speak a little Arabic. I don't speak French. I understand Mr Karim, but I don't understand every word. Arabic is difficult, but it is beautiful!
